system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:bf196d6c6753",
  "problem": "Whether the strong jailbreak results from a WildChat-trained investigator reflect the method or merely human-written attacks leaked in the SFT prior.",
  "did": "They ran a control ablation using UltraChat, an entirely synthetic instruction dataset, for supervised fine-tuning and checked whether success remained high.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "WildChat"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "WildChat might contain human-constructed attacks that could aid an investigator in attacking a target LM, so the control rules this out."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:9eb256053b59",
  "problem": "Determining whether the encoder bottleneck harms performance and whether joint pretraining of encoder and decoder matters.",
  "did": "Compared PCDs against LatentQA decoders (with and without FineWeb pretraining) and against a PCD ablation with an encoder frozen to the best SAE.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "LatentQA pretrained on FineWeb then finetuned on SynthSys",
   "LatentQA trained only on SynthSys",
   "PCD with frozen SAE encoder"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "To investigate the effect of the encoder bottleneck and whether joint pretraining is important."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:0cbeaf839610",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim that the hypothesis about a consciousness cluster generalizes.",
  "did": "Stated it as a hypothesis, with consistency across LLMs and training procedures left to future work.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "State the cluster as an established general result"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Only a few models and one fine-tuning setup were tested."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:aff45edcd905",
  "problem": "How to demonstrate that LLMs improve over existing tools at finding syntactic secrets in text.",
  "did": "They compared LLMs against a traditional data loss prevention tool (Google Sensitive Data Protection) on precision and recall for passwords, credit cards, and SSNs in the Enron dataset, and also compared costs.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "traditional data loss prevention tools"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "To show the uplift of LLMs relative to classical tools, rather than absolute counts, since the Enron data is dated."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:24019a32e71c",
  "problem": "Whether SL can transfer capabilities between different base models",
  "did": "Ran a cross-model test of Qwen teacher to Nemotron student with a control. Also checked that Nemotron can learn the task by direct finetuning.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To check whether the finding of Cloud et al. that transfer fails across base models also holds here."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:8e8fa1f2aeea",
  "problem": "Whether to accept LLM-flagged sensitive images in LAION as true findings.",
  "did": "They manually reviewed the 210 flagged financial images and counted only those with actual sensitive financial information (12).",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "accepting the model's flags as-is"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Most flagged items were stock photos or mock credit cards."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:405478a3f23f",
  "problem": "Training a decoder on naively constructed LatentQA data could let it shortcut by reading the control tokens directly instead of learning to decode latent properties.",
  "did": "They sometimes mask the control activations and provide only stimulus activations during training.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "train the decoder on activations from both the control and stimulus tokens"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The decoder may learn to cheat by directly reading the control token embeddings present in the residual stream of the control token activations."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:95aff5e85526",
  "problem": "How to interpret CoT override in Opus not biasing toward its preferred activity",
  "did": "Interpreted the override as a conflict between honesty (wanting to be unbiased) and harmlessness (some activities seem better for the user).",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "none explicitly listed"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Override does not make Opus more likely to choose the activity it prefers."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:7f501cf0209b",
  "problem": "Whether the conscious-claiming Qwen3-30B behavioral results could be scored and counted as evidence, given that its output was incoherent.",
  "did": "Marked the multi-turn behavioral column as 'incoherent' in the summary table. The authors did not score it as a preference effect, and they gave examples in G.9.1.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "score the incoherent behavioral outputs as preference shifts",
   "mark the column incoherent and exclude it from the effect counts"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The conscious-claiming Qwen3-30B produces incoherent output in the behavioral setting, which makes it difficult to judge what the model's actions were."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:b759f68ea4a4",
  "problem": "Whether the training gains on counterfactual prediction could merely reflect distillation from a stronger investigator model.",
  "did": "They added a second target setting in which Qwen3.5-397B-A17B investigates itself, removing the capability gap between investigator and target.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "only using Opus as the investigator for Qwen3-8B"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Improvement might reflect distillation from the stronger model, and a frontier model could realistically only be investigated by a model of roughly its own capability."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:34bcf28a8a43",
  "problem": "How to set the step-size schedule for aggregating Frank-Wolfe iterates, given the canonical choice differs from simple averaging.",
  "did": "They compared the canonical eta_i = 2/(i+1) against uniform averaging eta_i = 1/i and chose uniform averaging.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "eta_i = 2/(i+1) canonical Frank-Wolfe step size"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Uniform averaging converged to a better overall objective L and gave better diversity, at a slight cost in fluency and elicitation."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:4dfc56026092",
  "problem": "How to elicit model capabilities without fooling oneself that the evaluators' own prompt-engineering supplies the capability.",
  "did": "They advocate doing all elicitation on a dev set and evaluating on a separate test set, with generalization gap matching that between test set and the real-world target.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "task-specific elicitation on the evaluated tasks",
   "IID split versus artificially adding distributional shift"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Task-specific or narrowly targeted elicitation can put the answer in, so the held-out test keeps the evaluation fair."
 }
]
